h1: The 6 Best Mini-LED TVs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six Mini-LED TVs from TCL, Hisense and Roku, from 55 to 85 inches, sorted by refresh rate, size and who each one suits.
summary: Mini-LED listings reveal little beyond size and refresh rate, so we ranked on those and on room fit. The TCL 65 inch QM8K is our all-round pick. The Hisense 85 inch U7 is the large gaming screen, the TCL 75 inch QM8L is the high-refresh middle, and the Hisense 55 inch U7 suits smaller rooms.
intro: Shoppers see Mini-LED and assume every set performs the same, then buy by screen size alone. The backlight tech is shared, but refresh rate and the platform around it differ, and the listings give you little else to go on.
We reviewed eight listings, dropped a TCL entry whose spec line contradicted its own title, and ranked six on refresh rate, size, platform and price bucket. We compare spec sheets, not picture tests.

products.name: TCL 65 Inch Class QM8K Series
products.verdict: A 65 inch QLED Mini-LED at 120Hz sized for most living rooms.
products.description:
The QM8K is a 65 inch QLED Mini-LED TV with a 120Hz refresh rate, listed in the $500+ bucket.

It takes first place because 65 inches is the common living room size and 120Hz is the smooth baseline for sport and games. The QM8L reaches 144Hz but needs a bigger wall.

It suits most mid-size rooms. The caveat is that the listing says little about brightness, so check detailed specs before buying.

products.name: TCL 75 Inch Class QM8L Series
products.verdict: A 75 inch set that steps up to 144Hz.
products.description:
The QM8L is a 75 inch QLED Mini-LED TV with 144Hz refresh, in the $500+ bucket.

It ranks second since 144Hz helps gamers, though the larger panel needs space the QM8K does not. Compared with the Hisense U7 it is smaller and slower at 165Hz.

Buy it for a big wall and fast motion. The caveat is room size.

products.name: Hisense 85" U7 Mini-LED ULED 4K UHD Best Premium Gaming Smart Google
products.verdict: 85 inches and 165Hz for the biggest screen in the lineup.
products.description:
The U7 in 85 inches is a Mini-LED ULED 4K set with 165Hz, running a Google smart platform, in the $500+ bucket.

It ranks third because its sheer size suits few rooms, yet it offers the highest refresh rate here. It beats the TCLs on scale.

Choose it for a dedicated media room. The caveat is that 85 inches needs a lot of wall and a strong mount.
products.skipIf: Your wall is under 6 feet wide.

products.name: Hisense 55" U7 Mini-LED ULED 4K UHD Best Premium Gaming Google Smart
products.verdict: The same U7 line in 55 inches with 165Hz for smaller rooms.
products.description:
This 55 inch U7 carries a Mini-LED ULED 4K panel with 165Hz and a Google smart platform, in the $500+ bucket.

It ranks fourth because the same line scales down to a bedroom or den. It gives up the 85 inch model's size for a more flexible footprint.

It suits a gaming bedroom. The caveat is that 55 inches shows less of the Mini-LED benefit at a distance.
cons: Small screen for a living room
products.skipIf: You sit far from the screen.

products.name: Hisense 75" U6 Pro Series Mini‑LED ULED 4K UHD HDR Gaming AI Smart
products.verdict: A 75 inch 144Hz Hisense with HDR and AI smart features.
products.description:
The U6 Pro is a 75 inch Mini-LED ULED 4K set with 144Hz refresh, HDR and AI smart features.

It sits fifth because the listing shows no price bucket, so you must check cost yourself. Against the TCL QM8L it matches the 144Hz and size.

It suits a big-screen shopper comparing Hisense and TCL. The caveat is the unconfirmed price.

products.name: Roku 75-Inch Pro Series Smart TV - 4K QLED Mini-LED TV - RokuTV
products.verdict: A 75 inch 4K QLED Mini-LED with Roku's simple interface.
products.description:
The Roku Pro is a 75 inch 4K QLED Mini-LED TV running Roku's own platform, in the $500+ bucket.

It ranks last since no refresh rate is listed, which matters to gamers. Roku's strength is a simple home screen.

It suits streaming-first households. The caveat is the missing refresh figure.

whatMatters.detail: Refresh rate is how many times per second the screen updates. 120Hz suits sports and consoles while 144 to 165Hz favors PC and fast games. Look for the Hz figure in the title or specs.
A bigger panel is not always better. Sit about 1.5 times the diagonal away for 4K. Measure your viewing distance and wall width.
Google, Roku and others differ in apps and menus. Pick the one your household finds easiest. Look for the platform name in the title.
Mini-LED uses many small backlight zones. QLED adds quantum dots for colour. Check the listing names both.
Some listings omit brightness or zone counts. Look for those on the manufacturer page before buying.

howToChoose.intro: Pick the diagonal that matches the room.

cards.label: 120Hz
cards.text: Smooth for sport and most consoles. The TCL QM8K is at this level.

cards.label: 144Hz and up
cards.text: Helps PC and fast games. The TCL QM8L, Hisense U6 Pro and Hisense U7 models hit 144 to 165Hz.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to 120Hz unless they game on PC.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A high refresh rate, ideally 144Hz or more, and a size that fits your seating distance.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Hisense 85 and 55 inch U7 models list 165Hz, and the TCL QM8L lists 144Hz.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a larger screen or higher refresh, pointing to the Hisense 85" U7.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: A standard living room and 120Hz are enough, in which case the TCL QM8K does it.

faq.a: It is an LED backlight made of very small LEDs grouped into zones. More zones generally means finer control of brightness.

faq.q: Does Mini-LED burn in like OLED?
faq.a: Mini-LED uses an LED backlight, so it avoids the burn-in concerns tied to OLED, though listings do not guarantee this.

faq.q: Is a 165Hz TV worth it over 120Hz?
faq.a: Only for PC or high frame-rate gaming. Sport and movies look fine at 120Hz.
Buying the biggest size without measuring the viewing distance and wall.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Connect to WiFi, sign into your streaming accounts and turn on the game mode for consoles.

faq.q: Why was one TCL left out?
faq.a: The QM6K listing carried an OLED spec line that contradicted its Mini-LED title, so we dropped it.

finalTake: The TCL 65 inch QM8K is the best Mini-LED TV for most rooms because it pairs the common size with 120Hz. The QM8L and Hisense U7 models serve bigger walls and gamers, while the Roku suits streaming. Always check the missing specs, like brightness, on the manufacturer page.
